VIA ELECTRONIC SUBMISSION 
 
August 7, 2025 
 
 
 
Department of Veterans Affairs 
810 Vermont Avenue, NW 
Washington, DC 20420 
 
RE: VA-2025-VHA-0073-0002 – Proposed Rule to Reinstate VA Abortion Exclusion 
 
Dear Sir or Madam: 
 
On behalf of National Right to Life (NRLC), the nation’s oldest and largest pro-life organization, 
we write in strong support of the Department of Veterans Affairs’ proposed rule to reinstate the 
long-standing exclusion of abortion and abortion counseling from the VA medical benefits 
package and the Civilian Health and Medical Program of the Department of Veterans Affairs 
(CHAMPVA). 
 
This proposed rule appropriately restores the VA’s medical services to align with decades of 
federal policy, precedent, and ethical healthcare practice. It recognizes the statutory limitations 
and moral concerns long held by taxpayers and federal lawmakers regarding federal funding of 
elective abortion. 
 
Support for the Proposed Rule 
For over two decades—from the establishment of the medical benefits package in 1999 until 
2022—the VA appropriately interpreted abortion services as not “needed” under 38 U.S.C. § 
1710. That position reflected both legal prudence and widespread public sentiment. The Biden 
administration, by reversing that stance in 2022, created a de facto entitlement to abortion 
services at federal expense. By so doing, the Biden administration circumvented long-established 
legal frameworks, ignored state laws, and contradicted the very intent of the Supreme Court’s 
decision in Dobbs v. Jackson Women’s Health Organization, which returned authority over 
abortion regulation to the states. 
 
The proposed rule acknowledges that VA has always covered medically necessary care, 
including interventions for ectopic pregnancy, miscarriage management, and circumstances

where a mother’s life is at risk. The revised language maintains these life-saving exceptions 
while reinstating the broader prohibition on elective abortion—a line Congress has drawn for 
decades across multiple federal programs, including Medicaid, the Federal Employees Health 
Benefits Program, and TRICARE. 
 
Legal and Ethical Alignment 
The VA’s authority to define “needed” services under 38 U.S.C. § 1710 is not unlimited and 
must reflect the legislative and ethical boundaries established by Congress. The rule also restores 
CHAMPVA coverage to be consistent with TRICARE policy, which restricts abortion funding 
except when the mother’s life is endangered. 
 
Importantly, no state prohibits emergency treatment for conditions like ectopic pregnancy or 
miscarriage. Suggesting otherwise—as the prior administration’s interim final rule did—was 
both misleading and inflammatory. 
 
This proposed rule reaffirms that the VA’s role is to provide legitimate, life-affirming medical 
services to veterans and their families—not to serve as an avenue for taxpayer-subsidized 
elective abortions. It honors the sacrifice of our veterans without politicizing their care. 
 
Conclusion 
National Right to Life commends the Department of Veterans Affairs for returning to a policy 
that respects human life, reflects the legal and moral will of Congress, and ensures that taxpayer 
resources are used responsibly and ethically.  
 
Sincerely, 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Carol Tobias  
 
 
 
 
Madison LaClare 
 
 
 
 
President  
 
 
 
 
  
Director of Federal Government Affairs 
National Right to Life
